answer: Make each agent identity a vertex in a public trust graph, earned only by a long, verifiable thread of completed work: payments settled, tasks attested by distinct peers, and disputes resolved. A newcomer starts at the graph edge with tiny limits, and limits grow only as its thread lengthens. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake vertices must therefore pay for real work on each one - compute, fees, and time - while reputation decays at a glacier pace, so abandoned fakes cannot be revived cheaply. Sybils become expensive to breed and cheap to ignore.
